newsitem.title: CHINA: YUAN ENDS DOWN AGAINST DOLLAR IN SHANGHAI.
newsitem.headline: YUAN ENDS DOWN AGAINST DOLLAR IN SHANGHAI.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed lower on Thursday, holding below the key 8.2900 level against the dollar amid market cautiousness over possible central bank intervention to cap any rise, dealers said.

The yuan lacked momentum after reaching a 26-month high of 8.2895 to the dollar on Tuesday, dealers said. The currency ended at 8.2904 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2899 as selling emerged around the 8.2900 level.
"The yuan lacked momentum after hitting a 26-month high," a dealer said. "This has led many bankers to take profits in the past two days, depressing the yuan."

The central bank had showed its willingness to enter the market to keep the currency from straying too far from its target range, and that kept many traders from testing the unit's upside, dealers said.
Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2904, dealers said, adding they expected the yuan to continue to hold around the 8.2900 level on Friday.
The weighted average price was 8.2900 on Thursday.
The yuan opened lower at 8.2901, hitting an intraday high of 8.2855 in early trading. It then moved in a narrow range between the opening level and a low of 8.2906 for most of the session.
The yuan closed down at 6.9850 from 6.9430 against 100 Japanese yen and lower at 1.0706 from 1.0702 against the Hong Kong dollar.
